question: What claim about the fate of one whose mind is fixed on that must hold for cutting to fail to sever it?
premises: One whose mind is fixed on that remains directed toward it.
A blow directed at the body does not reach what lies beyond that fixation.
The effect of cutting fails to take hold when attention is fully absorbed elsewhere.
inference: Cutting cannot sever one whose mind is gone to that, just as a blow misses its mark under such absorption.
uncertainties: Extent of absorption required for the effect to fail is not specified.
plain_english: Even if one is being cut, one whose mind is fixed on that is not cut, just so.
